scope: Separately labelled development and final-candidate diagnostics; no elapsed-acceptance claim and no replacement of either full timing series.

object-runtime-cross.scope: Direct lli 2x2 of already optimized module versus runtime library; no driver/cache replacement; not acceptance evidence

object-generic.scope: Frozen generic compiler source with no LLVM treatment; emitted-code and elapsed confirmation before the new full series

object-normal-driver-capture.method: Read fd9 optimized bitcode, fd8 runtime DSO and live executable mapping bytes from an owned normal-driver child through procfs; no lli wrapper, input rewrite, compiler/LLVM/cache-setting change. The observer perturbs scheduling, so capture times are diagnostic only.
object-normal-driver-capture.limits: One capture per variant; establishes bytes and placement for those executions, not identical physical placement, cache state, CPU frequency or host execution conditions across all timed processes.

object-normal-driver-scheduling.method: One separate balanced 32-process object-JIT control using the full-series normal driver, exact source path, LLVM path, cache settings and environment. External observer pinned CPU8 samples the owned CPU0 child's schedstat from lli exec through zombie exit, without modifying its timers or code.
object-normal-driver-scheduling.scope_limit: Entry-to-exit counters cover the whole lli process segment including LLVM startup and untimed warmup; they cannot be aligned to individual kernel calls because piped stdout is buffered. Scheduler accounting updates can lag sampling. Negligible in-guest runqueue wait does not establish a CPU-frequency or host cause.
object-normal-driver-scheduling.disposition: Diagnostic only; does not replace the full-series +10.22% candidate object JIT regression, and elapsed acceptance remains open.
